top5.title: SEC investigates Nvidia’s accounting
top5.description: The U.S. SEC has opened a civil investigation to determine whether Nvidia misled investors about its accounting, without currently accusing the company of breaking the law. The investigation focuses in part on its sales to Singapore and on a customer suspected of rerouting chips to China.
top5.why: The SEC’s investigation into Nvidia’s accounting and possible China-linked chip rerouting could materially affect the world’s most valuable AI company, its valuation and semiconductor export controls.

top5.title: Trump threatens to tax data centers built overseas
top5.description: Donald Trump said U.S. companies would be barred from building data centers overseas or would have to pay a very high tax. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle already operate data centers in other countries.
top5.why: Trump’s threat to tax or restrict overseas data centers could reshape how major U.S. technology companies deploy global AI infrastructure and increase costs across the industry.

top5.title: YouTube nears $3 billion settlement with U.S. schools
top5.description: YouTube is close to a settlement worth up to $3 billion with school districts accusing it of designing an addictive platform. The settlement would also include new protection measures, which have not yet been specified.
top5.why: A potential $3 billion YouTube settlement would be one of the largest technology-platform liability deals and could bring significant new protections for children and teenagers.

top5.title: Amazon tells defense teams to automate after China-linked intrusion
top5.description: Amazon asked its defense teams to automate their processes after China-linked AI agents compromised a campus.
top5.why: The China-linked intrusion into an Amazon defense campus highlights the growing ability of AI-enabled attackers to penetrate sensitive systems and is prompting major changes in defense-sector operations.

top5.title: Gemini can now handle multistep everyday tasks
top5.description: Google has expanded Gemini’s Tasks mode to perform tasks such as scheduling appointments, reviewing bills and placing grocery orders. The service asks for confirmation before certain critical steps, but Google recommends checking the results.
top5.why: Gemini’s ability to schedule appointments, review bills and place orders signals that consumer AI is moving from answering questions toward executing multistep actions in the real world.
